answer: The registry bonds one sparrow to each applicant, trained six weeks to home to a ledge roost of its own. At dawn the registry names a bearing toward the horizon and releases the bird; the holder photographs it landing back on its ledge, and the next bearing comes from that landing photo and the holder's seal, so a replayed photo fails. One extra identity needs its own sparrow: $270 to train and band, plus six handler-weeks. To field 5,000 fakes, a farm must raise 5,000 birds: $1.35 million and 30,000 handler-weeks — no trainer teaches one bird two routes, and no roost holds two birds.
